arguments.content:
"""Order-preserving de-duplication."""

from __future__ import annotations


def dedupe_words(words, *, case_sensitive=True):
    """Return a new list with duplicates removed, keeping first occurrences.

    Args:
        words: Any iterable of words to de-duplicate. Consumed exactly once.
        case_sensitive: When False, words that differ only by case (compared
            with ``str.lower``) count as duplicates and the first spelling seen
            is kept.

    Returns:
        A new list of the de-duplicated words, in their original order. The
        input iterable is never modified.
    """
    seen = set()
    result = []
    for word in words:
        key = word if case_sensitive else word.lower()
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            result.append(word)
    return result

cd /workspace/repo && python - <<'EOF'
from textkit.dedupe import dedupe_words

# Never modifies argument
words = ["a", "b", "a"]
r = dedupe_words(words)
assert words == ["a", "b", "a"]
assert r == ["a", "b"]
assert r is not words
assert isinstance(r, list)

# Tuple accepted
t = ("a", "b", "a")
assert dedupe_words(t) == ["a", "b"]
assert t == ("a", "b", "a")

# Generator accepted
gen = (w for w in ["a", "a", "b"])
assert dedupe_words(gen) == ["a", "b"]

# One-shot iterator
assert dedupe_words(iter(["x", "y", "x"])) == ["x", "y"]

# Case-insensitive
assert dedupe_words(["Apple", "apple", "APPLE"], case_sensitive=False) == ["Apple"]

print("all good")
EOF
